input: An amine absorption unit was tested at pilot scale on gas from a cement kiln. Pilot scale places the unit somewhere between the laboratory and a full installation: the gas is the kiln's own gas, and the quantities involved are large enough to expose the solvent to the stream that it would treat in service. Over a period of 45 days at 11 t of carbon dioxide per day, the unit captured 85% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas. The steam demand was 3.3 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, and the solvent loss was 1.4 kg per tonne captured. It is important to note that the three figures describe the same run: the capture of 85% was achieved at the stated steam demand and solvent loss over the 45 days, and the steam figure represents the price of the capture in energy terms, paid in the regeneration of the solvent that the absorption process requires. The solvent loss is stated per tonne captured, which means that it scales with the amount treated rather than with the size of the unit. Beyond 45 days, however, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent remains untested. The reported performance is therefore a 45-day performance; whether capture, steam demand and solvent loss would hold as the solvent ages in contact with kiln dust lies outside the test, and a longer run is the measurement that would be needed in order to settle it.
